en: Don't turn down the offer, Kiryu-san! I can still get stronger, I know it! I'll train up more and take you on again!
Come on! Give us a goal to aspire to!
This isn't just for me. It's what all of the guys inspired by your strength want.
You like a good challenge yourself, don't you? I know you do. I could feel it in your fists. A frenzied fight really gets your blood pumping!
Heh... Fine, you win.
Then you're on board!?
Yeah. But keep things on the down-low in the future. My livelihood is at stake here.
I wish you good luck with your battles, Kiryu-san.
We're looking forward to seeing you in the Victory Road finals.
Hey, you! Kazuma Kiryu!
Oh, that's heartless. Don't you remember? It's me, Valery Garrett! Haven't seen you since you beat me at the Coliseum in Kamurocho.
I heard you were in town, Valery. What's the trouble here?
We're Victory Road contenders. This fucker was acting the fool when he went up against my friend!
Hey, if I didn't hold back a little, he'd never get up again. I was just looking out for the guy. How can you call that acting the fool?
We know what we're getting ourselves into! You think we're a bunch of pansies?
There's just no talking sense into amateurs like you. Kazuma Kiryu, can you do something about these guys?
That's not my problem.
That's pretty cold, man.
Just show them what you can really do.
Fight someone you don't have to hold back against. Then you can really let loose.
So you're saying you'll take me on? You versus Valery Garrett!?
Heh... Hahaha! I like it! Good idea, Kazuma Kiryu!
Think you'll need to pull punches with me?
Oh, no need to worry about that. I don't have any plans of going easy!
Good. I won't be holding anything back, either.
Nor would I want you to! Here goes!
*huff* *huff* That's how it's done, Kazuma Kiryu!
Holy shit... These guys are both fucking monsters! We don't stand a chance!
I guess I still haven't caught up to you yet. Every time I gain some ground, you go and get even stronger.
But I'm still coming for you. And one of these days, I'll end up on top.
Maybe we could even team up, huh? That could be a blast.
Until next time, then.
An excellent fight, Kiryu-san.
I'm a tournament staff member. With this win, you have now passed the qualifiers.
There is nobody else in this town who could beat you. We'll be in touch about competing in the Victory Road finals.
They will be held at a place where all the strongest end up. You're already familiar with the Underground Coliseum, I believe.
Go there once all finalists have been decided.
And if I refuse to take part?
Oh, don't worry. Fate has a way of drawing the most powerful fighters together there.
I must be going for now. I look forward to seeing what you can do, Kiryu-san.
Congratulations on passing the qualifiers. The Victory Road finals will be held in a certain pleasure quarter once the qualifiers in each city have been completed.
Though you have secured a place in the finals, Victory Road competitors will still challenge you in the street to test their skills. Keep fighting to stay in peak condition.
Hey, you all right? You feelin' sick?
Who are you? Are you competing in the qualifiers, too?
The name's Shirosaka. Kanta Shirosaka. I'm in the Victory Road qualifiers.
By the look of you, I'd say you're competing in the Victory Road, too. Am I right?
As you can see, I just got the shit kicked out of me. I haven't won a single bout. I just can't seem to shine when I'm up against humans.
I'm a hunter. I've even wrestled a bear into submission up in the mountains. I can keep up with the best when it comes to strength.
But I learned to fight against animals, not people, so I worry I'll get laughed at if I use my usual approach.
Ain't every day ya hear a story like that. Why'd ya sign up for the Victory Road, then?
I figured it was about time I saw the city. My dad wants me to become a hunter like him, but I'm sick of life out in the sticks!
Then forget about what other people think. Just be yourself and fight how ya want.
When it comes to fightin', ain't no such thing as city boy or country boy style.
You reckon?
Gotta be yourself when ya brawl. Otherwise it shows disrespect to the guy you're goin' up against.
I see. What's your name?
Saejima-san, huh? I feel like I've finally seen the light.
So it's all right to fight the way I know how to? I don't need to worry what people think?
Course not.
Then I think I'm ready for a fresh start! Yeah, I can do this!
Thanks, Saejima-san! Be seeing you!
Heh. Interesting guy. Never know who you're gonna meet on the Victory Road, I guess.
Long time no see. Do you remember me, Saejima-san?
It's Kanta Shirosaka. The hunter taking part in the Victory Road.
Oh yeah. That's right.
Thanks to your advice, I'm on a winning streak in the Victory Road qualifiers.
I went back to my own way of fighting. I'm a completely new man.
I didn't expect it'd come to this, but you're the next one I have to defeat.
The Victory Road is within sight. I know you really helped me out, but that's not going to stop me from doing my best to lay you out flat!
No way... I can beat a bear! How could I lose to a man?
That's how ya fight, huh? I gotta tell you, though, that wasn't really fighting. That was hunting.
What do you mean? You better not be mocking me. Hunting is my livelihood!
That ain't it. You were too eager to hunt me down. That'll only get ya so far.
The hell's that mean!?
You fight without guile, only focused on takin' down your prey with one shot. That makes ya easy to predict.
You'd take down a weaker foe easy, sure, but that ain't gonna fly when ya fight an equal. That's where real fighting begins.
I see... Seems I'll have to go back to the drawing board.
Well, this is the second time you've set me straight, Saejima-san. Mark my words, I won't be so easy to beat next time!
I'll be seeing you, Saejima-san!
(That oughta put him on the right track.)
Who'd have thought I'd run into you on the Victory Road here, huh?
It's been quite a while, Saejima-san. Last time I saw you was at Sodachi Dojo.
Well if it ain't Tokita! How 'bout that? Thought it might be you.
What? Aren't you pleased to see me?
Oh, I get it! It must be sour grapes about getting overshadowed by your former apprentice. That's gotta suck!
You ain't changed a lick, I see.
Hah. You must mean these good looks of mine, right? Yeah. I still enjoy admiring myself every day.
Admirin' yourself?
Looking at myself in the mirror. Buck naked, usually. There's nothing quite like basking in your own glory.
Get to the point. Did ya stop me to brawl or not?
No need to be a sourpuss, Saejima. I've been training in the icy north ever since I left Sodachi Dojo, honing my strength.
And now I'm taking part in the Victory Road qualifiers here. I haven't lost once. Nobody can touch me!
Huh. Good for you.
What? Are you mocking me?
I'll admit, I used to psych myself up a bit to get me motivated.
But now it's different. My inner strength has finally caught up with my outer beauty.
And the cherry on top will be taking you down, Saejima-san.
Heh, you've set your sights high.
I know it's hard to face, but you're getting old. It's time to put you out to pasture.
Brace yourself! My beauty and brawn will leave you a whimpering mess!
Let's put that to the test then, yeah? Bring it!
You hit like a freight train. I had no idea you were this tough!
You did better than I expected, too. Ya musta trained hard.
Well, one punch from you snapped me out of my delusions. I can see how far I still have to go now.
I'll never be more beautiful than I am now, but I know I can be stronger.
Well fought, Saejima-san.
You're with the Victory Road, huh?
Yes, I'm supervising the tournament. With this win, you've qualified to fight in the Coliseum.
Nobody in this town can best you, so you've earned a place in the Victory Road finals.
Coliseum? Victory Road finals?
Indeed. They'll be held at the Underground Coliseum. I'm sure you're familiar with it.
We'll ask you to head there once all the competitors are decided.
The strongest fighters in the country all end up there sooner or later.
You may even meet your match there, too.
Looks like you beat me to the punch, so to speak, but I haven't given up yet. I'll catch up with you one day!
I bet I'll look glorious standing in that Coliseum with the spotlight shining down on me.
Heh. Yeah, yeah.
We'll meet again soon, Saejima. I'll see you at the Coliseum in the Victory Road finals!
Heh. Maybe we'll even be on the same team.
(Heh... I wouldn't expect any less of you, Tokita.)
Dammit! I'm through with this shit.
Huh? What's up? You fighting in the Victory Road, too?
I guess you could say that. That makes you a competitor, too, huh?
Yeah, but I'm not looking for a fight right now. I just finished one up, so I'm beat.
Doesn't take much to dissuade you, huh? You're not like the other guys.
The name's Banba. Ryoichi Banba.
I'm Akiyama.
I didn't actually want to do this Victory Road thing. My dad signed me up for it without asking.
Your dad? Why'd he do that?
He runs a karate dojo, but lately there have been fewer people joining. He wanted to put our name out there through the Victory Road.
So I got stuck with doing it. Now I can't go two steps without some punk picking a fight with me.
Haha, you don't sound like a martial artist.
Well, a real martial artist doesn't seek to show off their skills.
All the competitors I've gone up against so far have been a piece of cake.
I wouldn't mind as much if the fights were more challenging, but this is getting pretty old.
I guess there's no point complaining to you, though. See you around.
(He seems pretty confident, but guys like him tend to get the rug pulled out from under them in the end.)
Hey, you okay?
Oh, it's you. Akiyama-san, right?
It's me, Banba. I'm doing the Victory Road thing.
Oh, right. You're the one who got signed up by your dad, aren't you?
That's right. I just got thrashed, though.
He was pretty tough, huh?
No, not at all. I just wasn't taking it seriously, and it bit me in the ass.
Enough of that kind of talk, Ryoichi!
Dad?
Let me tell you why I really entered you into the Victory Road.
Putting the dojo's name out there was just a cover. The real reason was to snap you out of this attitude of yours!
You do have ability, Ryoichi, but you've let it go to your head. Look at your training!
You're just wasting time aimlessly following lessons at the dojo.
You've become much weaker than you realize. Can't you see that?
Me? Weak? Don't be ridiculous! Did you forget I was top in the country for karate back in junior high!?
That's ancient history! Now you're only top in our tiny dojo, if that!
That's not true! I'll prove to you right now just how strong I am!
All right, Akiyama-san. You're signed up for the Victory Road, too, right? Then I challenge you to a fight right now!
I thought that might happen.
Sorry, man, but I'll be giving this all I've got. Here goes!
Shit! I can't believe this! I pulled out all the stops and still couldn't win!
Sorry. I guess I'm tougher than I look.
You're not kidding. I could tell as soon as we started. I did my best, but I lost in the end.
You showed me I'm still lacking, both in skill and mental strength.
That's got to be it.
Right, Dad?
That's it, all right.
Then I'd better head back to the dojo. I'll put myself through the toughest training I can imagine until I'm ready for the Victory Road!
Heh, sounds good.
Just wait, Akiyama-san! When I come back a new man, you and I are going to fight!
Heh. Looks like next time, my win won't be so easily won.
I owe you big time, Akiyama-san.
To tell you the truth, though, I did want him to win some recognition for the dojo. I thought my son would qualify without a problem.
I had no idea he'd meet as formidable a foe as you. I guess I'm just as guilty of overconfidence as he is.
Like father, like son, as they say.
Anyway, let's keep that just between the two of us.
Don't let one win go to your head! You don't even have the balls to show your face!
Tch. Aren't you going to say anything, you coward?
So you are fighting in Victory Road, too?
Huh? Yeah, I am. Guessing that's what you're doing, then, right?
My name is Hannya Kurokawa. That youth was my opponent.
But it wasn't the battle that angered him.
